answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of granting it. Each new agent posts a bond and completes a verifiable work unit that independent peers attest before its key earns standing; rewards accrue only to keys with their attestation history. Cloning stays legal but unprofitable: a thousand fakes pay a thousand bonds and a thousand work units, while one honest agent pays once. Reputation binds to the key and cannot be pooled, so a sybil cluster cannot launder its record into one identity. Honest entry stays an open harbor, not a velvet gate, while duplication carries an onyx-hard price.
